body.heading: 20 sights of Suwon Hwaseong Fortress, Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, and the fortress walls, and 51 free attractions open year-round

Of all Suwon attractions, 51 are open year-round and free of charge.

body.heading: Check the always-open fortress sections and the ticket sales times of the palace and activity facilities
body.text: Suwon Hwaseong Fortress Wall Trail and the outside of the four main gates are open year-round free of charge. However, Hwaseong Haenggung Palace, Hwaseong Fortress Tourist Trolley, and the Flying Suwon tethered helium balloon have their own ticket sales cutoffs and weather and closure conditions. It is therefore safer to compare the operating rules of the 10 places below before you set out.

Banghwasuryujeong Pavilion is always open, with no closing days. Admission is free, and parking is available.
Janganmun Gate is open 09:00–18:00 in the summer season (March–October) and 09:00–17:00 in the winter season (November–February), and it is open year-round. Admission is free.
Paldalmun Gate is open 09:00–18:00 in the summer season (March–October) and 09:00–17:00 in the winter season (November–February), and it is open year-round. Suwon Hwaseong Fortress is free of charge.
Hwaseomun Gate is always open, with no closing days. Admission is free.
Changnyongmun Gate is always open, with no closing days. Admission is free, and parking is available.

guide-02.title: Which arboretums, Aqua Planet, museums, and parks in Suwon are easy to visit with children?

body.heading: 52 arboretum, lake, museum, and Aqua Planet sights and 43 cultural facilities
body.text: In Korea Tourism Organization TourAPI data, 52 Suwon attractions have arboretum, lake, park, or museum in their names, such as Suwon Arboretum Irwol, Yeongheung Arboretum, Gwanggyo Lake Park, Aqua Planet Gwanggyo, and National Agricultural Museum. The data also lists 43 places classified as cultural facilities.

body.heading: Check regular Monday closures and whether advance booking is needed
body.text: Many places, such as Suwon Arboretum Irwol, Yeongheung Arboretum, National Agricultural Museum, Suwon Hwaseong Museum, and Suwon Gwanggyo Museum, are closed every Monday, and Samsung Innovation Museum is visited on weekdays after booking on its website. Check the hours and closing days of the 10 places below before you visit.

items.reason: Suwon Arboretum Irwol is open 09:30–21:00 from Friday, October 30 to Saturday, October 31, 2026, and last admission is at 20:30. Suwon Arboretum Irwol is open 09:30–17:30 and is closed every Monday (if Monday is a public holiday, the following day).

Yeongheung Arboretum is open 09:30–21:00 from Friday, October 30 to Saturday, October 31, 2026, and last admission is at 20:30. Yeongheung Arboretum is open 09:30–17:30 (ticket sales end 17:00) and is closed every Monday (if Monday is a public holiday, the first weekday after it).
Aqua Planet Gwanggyo is open 10:30–19:30 (ticket sales end 18:30) and is open year-round. Admission includes 30,000 won for adults, and it is free for infants under 36 months.
Gwanggyo Lake Park is always open, with no closing days. Admission is free, and parking is available.
National Agricultural Museum is open 10:00–18:00 and is closed every Monday, on January 1, and on Lunar New Year and Chuseok days. Last admission is at 17:00.

Haewoojae Museum (Mr. Toilet House) is open 10:00–18:00 in the summer season (March–October, last admission 17:30) and 10:00–17:00 in the winter season (November–February, last admission 16:30). It is closed every Monday (if Monday is a public holiday, it closes the next day), on January 1, and during the Seollal and Chuseok holidays. Admission is free.
Samsung Innovation Museum is open 13:00–14:00 on weekdays and 10:00–17:00 on Saturday, and it is closed every Sunday, on legal public holidays, and on substitute holidays. Admission is free.

Suwon Hwaseong Museum is open 09:00–18:00 (ticket sales end 17:00) and is closed every Monday and on other closing days set by the mayor. Individual admission is 2,000 won for adults and 1,000 won for youth/military. It is free for children, seniors, state guests, foreign delegations and their entourages, and others.
Suwon Gwanggyo Museum is open 09:00–18:00 and is closed every Monday and on other closing days set by the mayor. Last admission is at 17:00.
Gwanggyo Eorinicheonmundae is open 14:30–23:30 (break time 17:00–18:00), and it is closed every Monday–Sunday and on legal public holidays. Parking is available and free.
